tasteReview.beats: Zillow Bend homes (zillow.com/bend-or) — this page wins on sourced freshness: every ledger row and the alert count carries a dated, named source ('as of Sep 14, 2026', 'regional MLS through Oregon Data Share'), which Zillow's directory does not show per-row; but Zillow's map draws real clickable neighborhood boundaries, which this page's blurred dot-cloud does not.

defects.finding: The Central Oregon map is a blurred point-density heatmap with floating text labels (Madras, Sisters, Bend, etc.) laid over dark smudges — there are no outlined, individually touchable town regions, so beat 1 of the competitive brief (towns as touchable regions) is not demonstrated; it reads as a pin-density map, not an atlas of places.

The opened 'Search a city with a published reading' control is a bordered input over a flat list with a single gray hover row on Bend — no selected-state check icon, no grouping, no keyboard-highlight treatment distinct from a plain filtered list, so it reads as a house dropdown wearing the combobox name rather than the catalog demo interaction.

The verdict is stated twice back to back in one line — 'Balanced market at 4.6 months · Balanced 4-6' — after the two bars and the number line have already shown the same 4.6-month reading twice, so the same single stat is restated four times in one section with no new information each time.

defects.section: Sticky bottom alert bar, all *-mobile375 shots
defects.finding: The dark '256 houses came on the market' banner is pinned to the bottom of every mobile capture (ledger, reveal, compare-open, supply) and permanently covers roughly the last quarter of the viewport, clipping the final visible ledger row and the map zoom controls behind it rather than appearing as a dismissible, scroll-aware toast.

defects.section: Source label, hero right column and supply section
defects.finding: 'Market Truth' is printed as the citation for the months-of-supply figure with no gloss for a visitor — it reads as an internal dataset codename rather than a source a buyer or seller would recognize as authoritative.

tasteReview.verdict: This is a page that has already fixed its own prior critique — the old bare-numeral ledger now carries a bar per row, a real reveal micro-chart, and a sourced 30-day alert count — but it stops at competent, not breathtaking: the atlas is a muddy dot-cloud instead of touchable town regions (competitiveBriefPass fails on beat 1), the combobox is demoMatch:false because it shows no catalog-grade selection affordance, and the months-of-supply section restates one number four different ways instead of adding new information. Fix the atlas into real regions and the combobox into the actual demo interaction before this clears Tip Ready.

competitiveBrief.source: Matt 2026-09-16: 'My city pages have to be special' (on /cities/sisters). The index is the door to every city page. Page to beat: a portal's city hub (Zillow / Redfin 'Bend OR real estate' and their Oregon city directories) — a search-results list with a map. We win on a DRAWN region with live counts per town, doors that are real pages, and a sourced months-of-supply reading, not a link farm. Evidence quotes required; a lone competitiveBriefPass boolean is refuse.
competitiveBrief.productLock: H1 opening; the regional Atlas in the fold with every recorded town as a touchable region; the alerts figure beside it with the region's real 30-day count; the months-of-supply drawing (two named bars) with the city overlay combobox; every city A–Z in one ledger with its live count as a bar and each row a door; the rest of each city's doors; the regional alerts sheet; edges. Navy and cream only.
competitiveBrief.refuse: A KPI hero. A Google default map. A link farm of city names with no figure. A synthesized zero for a city with no published count (absent is not zero). Portal search chrome. Deleting the drawing or the ledger rows to satisfy a finding.

beats.text: The fold opens on Central Oregon drawn: an Atlas with every recorded town outlined as a touchable region, live listing marks inside, and a figure beside it — not a supply lecture on a cream column.

The alerts ask sits beside the drawing in the first viewport, with the region's real 30-day new-listing count as its claim and a sourced, dated line; the ask renders without a figure when none is published.

Months of supply is drawn as two named bars with a plain caption and a verdict that matches the number (≤4 seller · 4–6 balanced · ≥6 buyer), and the city overlay is a real, visible combobox — an open state is captured.

Every city, A to Z, in one ledger: each row a door to its own page, its live single-family count drawn as a bar, its median ask, and a reveal (verdict or twelve-month closes) where Market Truth publishes one.
Every figure names its source and window (live MLS through Oregon Data Share; Market Truth region row) — no count without a source, no zero for an unpublished city.
The page is crawlable as a directory: a CollectionPage ItemList of the featured cities, real anchors for every city row, breadcrumb, and the same H1 the title promises.
Beyond the fold the doors are real: each featured city's deep filter doors, the regional alerts sheet, and edges to communities, neighborhoods, subdivisions and the search.

Catalog controls are the demo interaction restyled navy/cream (the combobox overlay, the live count), and the 375 viewport shows the supply scale whole — nothing clipped, nothing that reads as a table wearing hairlines.
